rulebook: Child Care Facility Handbook (December 2025), incorporated by reference in Rule 65C-22.001, F.A.C. (rule eff. 9/1/2026), together with Chapter 65C-22, F.A.C. (Child Care Standards) and ss. 402.302 and 402.305, Florida Statutes (2026)

findings.requirement: At least one week before a change of ownership, custodial parents or legal guardians must be notified by posted notice, newsletter, or individual letters or flyers.
findings.quote: At least one week prior to changing ownership of a child care facility, in compliance with Section 402.305, F.S., one of the following methods of notification to custodial parents or legal guardians must be observed
findings.explanation: The handbook does not explain how parents will be notified at least one week before a change of ownership.
findings.fix: If our center ever changes ownership, we will let you know at least one week ahead by posting a notice at the center, including it in a newsletter, or sending a letter or flyer home.

findings.requirement: Children must never be left without child care personnel supervision inside or outside the facility, in a vehicle, or at a field trip location.
findings.quote: Children must never be left without child care personnel supervision inside or outside the facility, in a vehicle, or at a field trip location.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never left without a teacher's supervision, whether inside, on the playground, in a vehicle, or on a field trip.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that children are never left without supervision in all of the places the rule requires.

findings.requirement: In mixed-age groups including children under 1 year, one personnel may supervise no more than four children of any age; with children 1 to under 2 years, no more than six.
findings.quote: In groups of mixed age ranges, where children under one year of age are included, one child care personnel must be responsible for no more than four children of any age group, at all times.
findings.handbook_quote: When a group includes an infant under 12 months, one teacher may care for up to six children, as long as no more than four of them are infants.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows up to six children total when an infant is in the group, but the rule limits the teacher to no more than four children of any age.
findings.fix: When a group includes a baby under 12 months, one teacher cares for no more than four children total, of any age. When a group includes a child from 12 to 24 months, one teacher cares for no more than six children total.

findings.requirement: A child may be released only to persons authorized in writing by the custodial parent or legal guardian, and the program must verify identity with picture identification.
findings.quote: A child shall not be released to any person other than the person(s) authorized or in the manner authorized in writing by the custodial parent or legal guardians.
findings.handbook_quote: We release your child only to you or to the people you have authorized in writing on the enrollment form. Every person picking up your child must show a photo ID, even after we get to know them.
findings.explanation: The handbook limits release to written authorizations and requires photo identification.

findings.requirement: During nap time, personnel must be within sight and hearing of all children, except children up to 24 months require direct supervision at all times.
findings.quote: During nap time, child care personnel must be within sight and hearing of all the children.
findings.handbook_quote: During rest time, at least one teacher stays within sight and hearing of all resting children, and the other staff needed for ratio remain in the building on the same floor. Children under 24 months are directly supervised at all times, including while they sleep.
findings.explanation: The handbook matches the nap supervision and direct supervision requirements for children under 24 months.

findings.requirement: Transportation services must be approved by the Department before transporting children, and vehicles must have approved child safety alarms.
findings.quote: Prior to transporting children, the facility must be approved by the Department to offer transportation services.
findings.handbook_quote: Mangrove Meadow is approved by the Department to provide transportation, and our van has a child safety alarm that reminds the driver to check every seat.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that transportation is approved and the vehicle has a child safety alarm.

findings.requirement: A transportation log must be maintained for all children transported, including names, departure and arrival times, and required signatures.
findings.quote: A log must be maintained for all children being transported in a vehicle or on foot away from and/or to the premises of the child care facility.
findings.handbook_quote: For every trip, by van or on foot, we keep a transportation log with each child's name and departure and arrival times, signed by the driver or walking teacher and by a second staff member who confirms every child has arrived safely.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes a transportation log with names, times, and required signatures.

findings.requirement: Each child with an allergy should have a written emergency care plan with allergen avoidance, treatment plan, and symptoms requiring medication.
findings.quote: Each child with an allergy should have a written emergency care plan that includes
findings.handbook_quote: Each child with an allergy needs a written emergency care plan that names the allergen and how to avoid it, gives the treatment steps with the names and doses of any medicines, and lists the symptoms that mean medicine should be given.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires a written allergy emergency care plan with the required details.

findings.requirement: Written parental permission must be obtained for field trips, and trip details must be posted at least two working days in advance.
findings.quote: The date, time, and location of the field trip must be posted in an easily seen location at least two working days prior to each field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: Before every field trip, we post the date, time, and location by the front desk the day before, and a quick verbal okay at drop-off is all we need for your child to go.
findings.explanation: The handbook posts field trip details only the day before and accepts verbal permission, but the rule requires posting at least two working days ahead and written parental permission.
findings.fix: We post the date, time, and location of each field trip in an easy-to-see place at least two working days ahead, and we get your written permission before your child goes.

findings.requirement: The center must adopt and give parents a written discipline policy consistent with the statute, including prohibited severe, humiliating, frightening, or food/rest/toileting-related discipline.
findings.quote: The child care facility shall adopt a discipline policy consistent with Section 402.305(12), F.S., including standards that prohibit children from being subjected to discipline which is severe, humiliating, frightening, or associated with food, rest, or toileting.
findings.handbook_quote: Our discipline is never severe, humiliating, or frightening, and it is never connected to food, rest, or toileting. Spanking and every other kind of physical punishment are prohibited.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes a written discipline policy with the required prohibited practices.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive a written copy of the center's disciplinary and expulsion policies, with receipt documented on the enrollment form.
findings.quote: Verification that the child care facility has provided the parent or guardian a written copy of the disciplinary and expulsion policies used by the program must be documented on the enrollment form with the signature of the custodial parent or legal guardian.
findings.handbook_quote: Before your child starts, we give you a written copy of these discipline and expulsion policies, and you sign the enrollment form to confirm you received them.
findings.explanation: The handbook provides written discipline and expulsion policies and documents receipt on the enrollment form.

findings.requirement: The current disciplinary and expulsion policies must be available for review by parents or legal guardians and the licensing authority.
findings.quote: A copy of the current disciplinary and expulsion policies must be available for review by the parents or legal guardian and the licensing authority.
findings.handbook_quote: A copy of our current discipline and expulsion policies is always kept at the front desk for parents and the licensing authority to review.
findings.explanation: The handbook makes the current discipline and expulsion policies available for review.

findings.requirement: Spanking or any other physical punishment is prohibited, along with isolation, binding, withholding food, and other listed practices.
findings.quote: Spanking or any other form of physical punishment is prohibited.
findings.handbook_quote: Spanking and every other kind of physical punishment are prohibited. Staff never hit, pinch, or roughly handle a child, never shame or threaten a child, and never use harsh or sarcastic words.
findings.explanation: The handbook prohibits spanking, physical punishment, and the other listed discipline practices.

findings.requirement: Active play must not be completely withheld from children who misbehave, and time-outs must be developmentally appropriate.
findings.quote: Active play, both indoor and outdoor, must not be completely withheld from children who misbehave.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never kept from active play for an entire play period because of misbehavior.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that active play is not completely withheld for misbehavior.

findings.requirement: Expulsion policies must be written, provided to parents, and available for review by parents and the licensing authority.
findings.quote: A copy of the current disciplinary and expulsion policies must be available for review by the parents or legal guardian and the licensing authority.
findings.handbook_quote: A copy of our current discipline and expulsion policies is always kept at the front desk for parents and the licensing authority to review.
findings.explanation: The handbook has written expulsion policies that are available for review.

findings.requirement: Programs caring for infants must have a written policy and procedure to identify and prevent shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma.
findings.quote: All programs that care for infants must have a written policy and procedure to identify and prevent shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include a written policy and procedure to identify and prevent shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma.
findings.fix: Because we care for infants, we keep a written policy and procedure to help identify and prevent shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma, and all staff who work with infants complete safe sleep training.

findings.requirement: Parents or guardians must be informed in writing of all animals on the premises.
findings.section: 3.1 General Health and Safety Requirements C
findings.quote: Parents/guardians must be informed in writing of all animals on the premises.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not tell parents in writing about animals on the premises.
findings.fix: If we have any animals at the center, we will tell you in writing, and we keep their current vaccination records available for review.

findings.requirement: Owners or operators must notify custodial parents and legal guardians in writing that smoking, including e-cigarettes and vaping, is prohibited on the premises.
findings.section: 3.1 General Health and Safety Requirements E
findings.quote: Owners/operators are to notify custodial parents and legal guardians, in writing, that smoking, including e- cigarettes and vaping, is prohibited on the premises of the child care facility.
findings.explanation: The handbook states the smoke-free policy but does not say parents are notified in writing.
findings.fix: We will notify you in writing that smoking, including e-cigarettes and vaping, is not allowed anywhere on our premises.

findings.requirement: Infants unable to roll over must be positioned on their backs on a firm surface, with no excess bedding in cribs or play yards.
findings.quote: When napping or sleeping, young infants who are not able to roll over must be positioned on their backs and on a firm surface to reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome, unless an alternate position is authorized by a physician.
findings.handbook_quote: Infants who cannot yet roll over may be placed to sleep on their tummies or sides if that is how they settle best at home.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows infants who cannot roll over to sleep on their tummies or sides, but the rule requires them to be on their backs unless a physician authorizes an alternate position.
findings.fix: Babies who cannot roll over yet are always placed on their backs on a firm surface for sleep, with no extra bedding in the crib.

findings.requirement: Cribs or play yards used by a child must be at least 18 inches from window blinds, draperies, or other strangulation hazards.
findings.quote: Cribs, playpens, play yards, other napping and sleeping bedding being used by a child must be placed a minimum of 18 inches away from window blinds, draperies or any window treatment/cover that pose a strangulation hazard.
findings.handbook_quote: Every crib sits at least 18 inches from window blinds and curtains.
findings.explanation: The handbook meets the required distance from window blinds and curtains.

findings.requirement: The operator must develop a written emergency preparedness plan covering fire, evacuation, relocation, shelter in place, lockdown, inclement weather, and parent reunification.
findings.quote: The operator must develop a written emergency preparedness plan that includes, at a minimum, procedures to be taken by the facility during a fire, evacuation, relocation, shelter in place, lockdown, and inclement weather
findings.handbook_quote: Our written emergency preparedness plan covers fire, evacuation, relocation, shelter in place, lockdown, and severe weather such as hurricanes and tornadoes.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes a written emergency preparedness plan covering the required situations.

findings.requirement: Fire drills using the approved alarm system must be conducted monthly at various dates and times when children are in care.
findings.quote: During the facility's license year, fire drills utilizing the alarm system, approved by the local fire authority, must be conducted monthly at various dates and times when children are in care.
findings.handbook_quote: We hold a fire drill twice a year, once in the fall and once in the spring, including one during nap time and one using an alternate exit route.
findings.explanation: The handbook holds fire drills twice a year, but the rule requires monthly fire drills at various dates and times when children are in care.
findings.fix: We practice a fire drill every month at different times, including one during nap time and one using a different exit route.

findings.requirement: Lockdown and inclement weather drills must be conducted at least once each per operating year when children are in care.
findings.quote: Lockdown and inclement weather drills shall be conducted a minimum of one time each per operating year when children are in care
findings.handbook_quote: We also practice a lockdown drill and a severe weather drill at least once each year.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that lockdown and severe weather drills are practiced at least once each year.

findings.requirement: The facility must have a written plan for reporting and managing incidents or unusual occurrences threatening health, safety, or welfare.
findings.quote: The facility must have a written plan for reporting and managing any incident or unusual occurrence that is threatening to the health, safety, or welfare of the children or child care personnel to the licensing authority.
findings.handbook_quote: We also keep a written plan for reporting and managing serious incidents, including a lost or missing child, suspected maltreatment, an injury or illness needing emergency treatment, the death of a child or staff member, or a threatening person trying to enter, and for reporting each to the licensing authority.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes a written plan for reporting and managing serious incidents.

findings.requirement: Foods associated with choking must not be served to children under 4, and food must be cut to required sizes for infants and toddlers.
findings.quote: Foods that are associated with young children's choking incidents must not be served to children under 4 years of age
findings.handbook_quote: For children under four, we do not serve choking hazards such as whole grapes, hot dog rounds, popcorn, nuts, or cheese cubes. We cut food for infants into pieces a quarter inch or smaller and food for toddlers into pieces a half inch or smaller, including food sent from home.
findings.explanation: The handbook prohibits choking hazards for children under four and uses the required food sizes.

findings.requirement: Hot foods must be maintained at 135 degrees or above and cold foods at 41 degrees or below to prevent food from becoming potentially hazardous.
findings.quote: To prevent food from becoming potentially hazardous, hot foods must be maintained at a temperature of 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above, and cold foods must be maintained at temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit, or below.
findings.handbook_quote: we hold hot foods at 135°F or above and cold foods at 41°F or below.
findings.explanation: The handbook maintains hot and cold foods at the required temperatures.

findings.requirement: The facility must have a written routine schedule for cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting equipment, materials, furnishings, and play areas.
findings.quote: Facilities must have a written routine schedule for cleaning, sanitizing and disinfecting equipment, materials, furnishings and play areas.
findings.handbook_quote: We also follow a written cleaning schedule posted in each room: tables, toys, sinks, toilets, diaper pails, and floors are cleaned and sanitized daily, and cribs, cots, mats, linens, and cloth toys are washed weekly.
findings.explanation: The handbook has a written routine cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting schedule.

findings.requirement: The facility must develop a written exposure plan for universal safety precautions and educate personnel before work and annually.
findings.quote: Child care facilities shall develop a written exposure plan regarding universal safety precautions, recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to follow in the event there is exposure to blood and potentially infectious fluids.
findings.handbook_quote: Our staff follow a written exposure plan based on CDC universal precautions for contact with blood or other body fluids, and every staff member is trained on it before starting work and again every year.
findings.explanation: The handbook has a written exposure plan and trains staff before work and annually.

findings.requirement: A child or person suspected of communicable disease must be removed or isolated until medically authorized or symptoms are no longer present.
findings.quote: Any child, child care personnel, or other person in the child care facility suspected of having a communicable disease must be removed from the program or placed in an isolation area until removed.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child must stay home, or will be sent home, with a temperature of 101°F or higher together with other signs of illness, diarrhea (more than one abnormally loose stool in 24 hours), severe or whooping cough, difficult breathing, a stiff neck, pink eye, open skin sores, or yellowish skin or eyes. A sick child rests in our isolation area, within sight and hearing of a staff member, until you arrive. Your child may return with a note from the doctor or once the symptoms are gone.
findings.explanation: The handbook excludes or isolates children with signs of communicable disease and allows return with medical authorization or when symptoms are gone.

findings.requirement: Signs such as fever of 101 degrees with illness, diarrhea, pink eye, or open lesions require exclusion or isolation.
findings.quote: Temperature of 101 degrees Fahrenheit or higher in conjunction with any other signs of illness
findings.handbook_quote: Your child must stay home, or will be sent home, with a temperature of 101°F or higher together with other signs of illness, diarrhea (more than one abnormally loose stool in 24 hours), severe or whooping cough, difficult breathing, a stiff neck, pink eye, open skin sores, or yellowish skin or eyes.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists signs and symptoms that require exclusion or isolation.

findings.requirement: A child with head lice may not return until the next day and only if treatment has occurred and been verified.
findings.quote: A child identified as having head lice must not be permitted to return until the following day, and then only if treatment has occurred and been verified.
findings.handbook_quote: A child with head lice may return the following day, once treatment has been done and verified with a product box or a signed note from you.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows return the following day only after treatment is verified.

findings.requirement: The operator must notify the local county health department immediately upon any suspected outbreak of communicable disease.
findings.quote: Operators are required to notify the local county health department immediately upon any suspected outbreak of communicable disease and must follow the health department's direction.
findings.handbook_quote: If two or more children show similar symptoms within 72 hours, or a reportable disease is suspected, we notify the county health department immediately and follow its direction.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires immediate notification of the county health department for a suspected outbreak.

findings.requirement: Emergency service telephone numbers, facility address, and directions must be posted on or near all telephones.
findings.quote: Emergency service telephone numbers must be posted on or near all telephones, including 911, ambulance, fire, police, poison control center, Florida Abuse Hotline, and the county public health department.
findings.handbook_quote: Emergency numbers, including 911, poison control, the Florida Abuse Hotline, and the county health department, are posted by every phone with our address and directions to the center.
findings.explanation: The handbook posts emergency numbers, address, and directions by every phone.

findings.requirement: Medication may be given only with dated, signed written authorization from the custodial parent or legal guardian containing child, medication, date, time, and dosage.
findings.quote: The child care program must have written authorization from the custodial parent or legal guardian to give prescription and non-prescription medications. This authorization must be dated and signed by the custodial parent or legal guardian and contain the child's name; the name of the medication to be given; and date, time and amount of the correct dosage to be given.
findings.handbook_quote: We give medication when you fill out our medication form or, if you are in a rush at drop-off, when you simply tell the teacher the name of the medicine and how much to give.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows medication to be given based on a verbal request at drop-off, but the rule requires dated and signed written authorization.
findings.fix: We give medicine only after you give us written permission that is dated and signed and lists your child, the medicine, and the date, time, and amount to give.

findings.requirement: Accidents and incidents threatening health, safety, or welfare must be documented the same day and shared with the parent or guardian that day.
findings.quote: All accidents and incidents or unusual occurrences that are threatening to the health, safety, or welfare of a child that occur while the child is in care must be documented on the same day they occur.
findings.handbook_quote: We write up every accident or incident on the same day it happens and share the report with you that same day.
findings.explanation: The handbook documents and shares accidents and incidents on the same day.

findings.requirement: In the event of serious injury or death, the incident must immediately be reported to the licensing authority.
findings.quote: In the event of serious injury or death, the incident must immediately be reported to the licensing authority.
findings.handbook_quote: Any serious injury is reported immediately to our licensing authority.
findings.explanation: The handbook reports serious injuries immediately to the licensing authority.

findings.requirement: Medication brought to the facility must be in the original container, with prescription labels showing physician or pharmacy, child, medication, and directions.
findings.quote: Prescription and non-prescription medication brought to the child care facility by the custodial parent or legal guardian must be in the original container.
findings.handbook_quote: All medicine must come in its original container, and prescription medicine must have the pharmacy label showing the doctor or pharmacy, your child's name, the medicine, and the directions.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires original containers and prescription labels with the required information.

findings.requirement: A medication record must document child, medication, date, time, amount, dosage, and the name and signature of the person who gave it.
findings.quote: The facility must maintain a record for each child receiving any medications that documents the full name of the child, the name of the medication, the date and time the medication was given, the amount and dosage, and the name and signature of the person who gave the medication.
findings.handbook_quote: Each dose is recorded with your child's full name, the medicine, the date and time, the amount, and the name and signature of the staff member who gave it.
findings.explanation: The handbook records each medication dose with the required details.

findings.requirement: Records must be maintained at the program location and available during hours of operation for review by the licensing authority.
findings.quote: Each of the records described in this section must be maintained at the program location and must be available during the hours of operation for review by the licensing authority
findings.handbook_quote: All required records are kept here at the center and are available to the licensing authority for review during our hours of operation.
findings.explanation: The handbook keeps required records at the center and available during operating hours.

findings.requirement: Each child must have a current Florida Certification of Immunization form or religious exemption on file.
findings.quote: The child care facility is responsible for obtaining for each child in care a current, complete and properly executed Florida Certification of Immunization form Part A-1, B, or C, DH 680
findings.handbook_quote: Within 30 days of enrollment, we need a current Florida Certification of Immunization (DH 680) or Religious Exemption from Immunization (DH 681), plus a Student Health Examination (DH 3040), which is valid for two years from the date of the physical.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires a current immunization form or religious exemption for each child.

findings.requirement: Each child must have a current Student Health Examination form, valid for two years from the physical date.
findings.quote: The child care facility is responsible for obtaining for each child in care a current, complete and properly executed Student Health Examination form DH 3040
findings.handbook_quote: Within 30 days of enrollment, we need a current Florida Certification of Immunization (DH 680) or Religious Exemption from Immunization (DH 681), plus a Student Health Examination (DH 3040), which is valid for two years from the date of the physical.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires a current student health examination valid for two years.

findings.requirement: If required immunization or health documentation is not provided within 30 days of enrollment, the child may not remain in the program.
findings.quote: If the custodial parents or legal guardians fail to provide the documentation required above within 30 days of enrollment, the facility shall not allow the child to remain in the program.
findings.handbook_quote: If these forms are not on file within 30 days, your child cannot continue to attend.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that a child cannot continue to attend if required forms are not on file within 30 days.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive the center's food and nutrition policies, including language on food safety and food allergens, with receipt documented.
findings.quote: The child care facility's food and nutrition policies that includes language on food safety and food allergens.
findings.handbook_quote: At enrollment you will receive the Department of Children and Families brochure Know Your Child Care Facility, our written discipline and expulsion policies, and our food and nutrition policies, which include our food safety and food allergen practices. You will sign the enrollment form to confirm that you received each of these.
findings.explanation: The handbook provides food and nutrition policies and documents receipt on the enrollment form.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive the Department's Know Your Child Care Facility brochure, with receipt documented on the enrollment form.
findings.quote: The Department's child care facility brochure, CF/PI 175-24, Know Your Child Care Facility, which is incorporated by reference in 65C-22.001(7)(l), F.A.C.
findings.handbook_quote: At enrollment you will receive the Department of Children and Families brochure Know Your Child Care Facility, our written discipline and expulsion policies, and our food and nutrition policies, which include our food safety and food allergen practices. You will sign the enrollment form to confirm that you received each of these.
findings.explanation: The handbook provides the required brochure and documents receipt on the enrollment form.

findings.requirement: Enrollment information must be obtained from the custodial parent or legal guardian prior to accepting a child in care.
findings.quote: The facility operator shall obtain enrollment information from the child's custodial parent or legal guardian prior to accepting a child in care.
findings.handbook_quote: Before your child's first day, you will complete the Child Care Application for Enrollment. We cannot accept a child into care until this information is on file.
findings.explanation: The handbook obtains enrollment information before accepting a child into care.

findings.requirement: Failure to perform mandatory reporter duties under Section 39.201, F.S., constitutes a violation of child care standards.
findings.quote: Failure to perform the duties of a mandatory reporter pursuant to Section 39.201, F.S., constitutes a violation of the standards in Section 402.301-.319, F.S.
findings.handbook_quote: Florida law makes every member of our staff a mandatory reporter. Any staff member who suspects that a child has been abused, abandoned, or neglected must report it right away to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-96-ABUSE. Telling the director does not replace this report.
findings.explanation: The handbook states mandatory reporting duties and that reporting to the director does not replace the report.

findings.requirement: Custodial parents or legal guardians must have reasonable access in person and by telephone during normal hours or while the child is in care.
findings.quote: A child care facility must provide the custodial parent or legal guardian access, in person and by telephone, to the child care facility during the facility's normal hours of operation or during the time the child is in care.
findings.handbook_quote: You are welcome at Mangrove Meadow at any time while we are open. You may visit, observe, or call the center whenever your child is in our care, and no appointment is needed.
findings.explanation: The handbook provides reasonable in-person and telephone access during operating hours.

findings.requirement: Daily attendance must be taken and recorded accurately, documenting the time each child enters and departs the program.
findings.quote: Daily attendance of children must be taken and recorded accurately by the child care personnel, documenting the time when each child enters and departs the program.
findings.handbook_quote: Please walk your child into the classroom and sign in with the time on the classroom tablet, then sign out with the time at pickup. Teachers check these entries so our attendance record is always accurate.
findings.explanation: The handbook records the time each child enters and departs the program.

findings.requirement: Staff-to-child ratios must follow the age-based minimums, including 1:4 for birth through 1 year and 1:25 for children 5 years and older.
findings.quote: For children from birth through 1 year of age, there must be one child care personnel for every four children.
findings.handbook_quote:
| Birth to 1 year | 1 : 4 | Minnows |
| 1 year to under 2 years | 1 : 6 | Tadpoles |
| 2 years to under 3 years | 1 : 11 | Sea Turtles |
| 3 years to under 4 years | 1 : 15 | Dolphins |
| 4 years to under 5 years | 1 : 20 | Manatees (VPK) |
| 5 years and older | 1 : 25 | Explorers |
findings.explanation: The handbook's age-based staff-to-child ratios match the required minimums.

summary: The handbook covers most required items, but it conflicts with the rules on mixed-age ratios, field trip notice and permission, infant sleep position, monthly fire drills, and verbal medication authorization. It also omits required written notices and policies for change of ownership, shaken baby syndrome, animals, and smoking.
